Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph shows a small, hyperlucent right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings and an elevated right hemidiaphragm, which are classic signs of unilateral absence of the right pulmonary artery (UAPA). This congenital anomaly is frequently associated with recurrent lung infections due to impaired clearance and collateral blood flow, as well as other congenital defects like laryngomalacia.
